#1351. McTominay and Anguissa: ‘Napoli can build momentum’ after 1-0 victory

Scott McTominay hopes Napoli can ‘get a bit of momentum going’ after his goal allowed them to beat Torino, while Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa insists ‘we can climb back up the table.’

It was a difficult match for the Partenopei, who struggled to break Toro down and also ran a risk when Ronaldo Mandragora thumped the crossbar from distance.

McTominay finally broke the deadlock with a strike from the edge of the area, set up for him by Noa Lang after a defensive run to win back the ball, turning it into an attacking situation.

The Scotland international has a real history against Torino, scoring four goals past them in only three meetings.

“In football it’s about the next game, and the next game, you have to do your best. We have a team that wants to work, wants to push, and we want to win more games,” McTominay told Sky Sport Italia.

Allegri turned to his bench after the goal and said: ‘See, they score when they smile, I told them to smile more.’

“I am feeling much better,” smiled McTominay.

“It’s an important goal, but more importantly we won, we had to win. I’m happy for the fans, we need to get a bit of momentum going, keep winning.”

Now there is a trip to Manchester City in the Champions League, which will feel like a derby for former Manchester United midfielder McTominay.

“A great game, we’ll recover now and then think about it from tomorrow.”

There had been some changes and tactical experiments, moving to a 3-5-2 formation, but Antonio Vergara limped off after just 11 minutes and is now expected to miss Tuesday’s Champions League trip to Manchester City.

Kevin De Bruyne had initially been rested with that in mind too, but had to come on to replace Vergara, meaning extra fatigue on 35-year-old legs.

“When you work as a team, it becomes easier for everyone,” added Anguissa.

“We know what Scott can do, we’re happy he scored and these are three very important points. We have to keep working together, it is the only way to get out of this situation. We are very concentrated and know what we need to do.

“It is important to think positive, take it one game at a time. I have faith, and I feel that this team can do anything. There’s a long way to go this season, we can climb back up the table.”

#1350. Celtic 4 St Mirren 1: Oxlade-Chamberlain rolls back the years as champions put Buddies to the sword

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

Despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

The outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

It’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win

On Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor showed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager showed up well.

#1349. Most Successful Clubs in World Football - Trophies and Honours

Success in football comes in circles, as good times come and go for every club, but some clubs have far more consistent cycles than others.

Many clubs have had generations of success through each era of football, through multiple competitions, managers, rule changes and players, as the cream always rises to the top.

The 2026-27 campaign got underway in August, but most of the trophies won't be dished out until the second half of the campaign.

As we deep dive into the stories of these footballing superpowers, it's essential to understand that every title, every cup, every league win has a backdrop. Stories of grit, magic moments, unforgettable comebacks, and yes, heartbreaks too. Every piece of silverware is a chapter in the illustrious book of their history.

Prepare for an exhilarating journey. A trip through football's hall of fame, where tales of dramatic finals, footballing dynasties, and players who've become larger than life await.

While trophies do stand testament to a club's success, it's the culture, the traditions, and the die-hard fans that truly capture its essence. As we profile these titans, we're not just tallying their victories but celebrating the undying spirit that's made them legendary. Because remember, in football, the journey is just as important, if not more, than the destination. Let the games begin.

Some of the biggest clubs in world football come from Britain - and the top 20 UK sides have been ranked.

Bulgarian powerhouse CSKA Sofia are first up on our list and are probably not the first club you would think of when it comes to success in football. Nevertheless, they have won an astonishing 57 trophies in their history - a legacy that few can rival in Eastern European circles.

Established in 1948, they have maintained a firm grip on domestic football in their nation, which has undoubtedly impressed fans and foes alike. Their fierce rivalries and iconic moments against the likes of Levski Sofia have left an indelible mark on the football world, known as "The Eternal Derby of Bulgaria."

Zamalek are certainly not a football team that rolls across the tongue as easily as some of the top sides in Europe do, but this team has, over the years, boasted an iron grip on domestic football in Egypt and have dominated the scene since the club was established in 1911.

They are not only a cornerstone of Egyptian football, but also for Africa as a whole. Their 58-trophy haul has been a testament to their resilience and consistency. The iconic Cairo derby between them and Al Ahly is a spectacle, a footballing carnival that never ceases to amaze. It has been branded in the past as "the world's most violent derby" - though, remarkably, Zamalek aren't the only Egyptian side on this list.

Founded in 1970, PSG are among the youngest clubs on this list. But after winning four trophies in the 2024/25 campaign - including their first-ever Champions League triumph - and then doing the same again just a season on, they have undoubtedly earned their place among the most prestigious and decorated clubs in the world.

Luis Enrique is building something truly magnificent in Paris, and Les Parisiens are certainly here to stay, boasting a young squad that includes the likes of Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Vitinha, and many others. Furthermore, having won 13 of the last 15 Ligue 1 seasons with relative ease, continued domestic dominance seems almost guaranteed.

FCSB might not mean a lot to some, but if you say Steaua Bucharest, then things start to make a lot more sense. FCSB's 62 trophies firmly entrench them as Romania's best club by far. The club isn't even 100 years old yet but has achieved more in Europe than other clubs in neighbouring countries could ever dream of. Steaua's European Cup win in 1986, otherwise known as the 'Miracle of 86,' is something that the club is incredibly proud of, and rightly so.

They went on to produce one of the longest unbeaten streaks that's ever been seen for the next three years. This club is the shining example of a true underdog. Even though they are the best team in their country by quite some distance, they are still considered minnows to the rest of Europe. That being said, with a European Cup to their name, their supporters would argue otherwise.

Boca Juniors are one of the most famous clubs in the world and arguably have a global reach that matches or exceeds some of the top sides in Europe. Their famous blue and yellow strips are synonymous throughout the world of football, especially for the performances of Diego Maradona - easily one of the greatest players of all time - though it has been a while since someone with that presence made an impact on the team.

The Argentine club secured their 62nd and most-recent trophy in November 2026, defeating Brazilian side Atletico-MG in the final of the CONMEBOL Sudamericana - South America's equivalent of the UEFA Europa League.

Galatasaray stand tall and proud as a symbol of Turkish footballing might. The cauldron of noise that is generated at their Turk Telekom Arena makes it a venue most European adversaries dread, a tale that has lived since the early 1990s when Manchester United visited for the first time - alongside a famous Tifo that stated: "Welcome to Hell."

But it's not only the Red Devils who have felt the wrath of the brilliant football club over the years. Because of the help from their passionate supporters, and the valiant efforts on the pitch in the club's famous red and yellow colours, they have clinched no more but no less than 64 trophies, their latest being yet another league and cup double, and they will continue to etch unforgettable memories into the history of Galatasaray.

Next up are the Belgian giants Anderlecht, who have remained competitive for as long as many of us can remember. It seemed like every year that they would face Manchester United in the Champions League, and there's a good reason for that: their unrelenting success on the domestic stage.

With 64 trophies to their name since their founding in 1908, this showcases how consistent they have been over the years in the Belgian Pro League and other cup competitions they are able to participate in. When football fans think of purple and white colours, the first club that comes to their head is Anderlecht.

Croatian giants Dinamo Zagreb are next up on the list, as one of the most well-known names in eastern European football. Their domination of Croatian football has seen them as regulars on the continental stage, although their European success has been sparse in recent years.

With 68 trophies, Dinamo are tied for major honours with arguably the biggest club in the world, Manchester United, and are the only Croatian club to have won a continental trophy, albeit when the nation was part of Yugoslavia, having won the 1966-67 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, beating Don Revie's Leeds United in the final, having beaten Juventus along the way.

If you say the 'Theatre of Dreams', Old Trafford, or the 'Busby Babes' to someone, there's only one club that comes to mind: Manchester United. Their 68 trophies paint a tale of legends, right from the 'Busby Babes' Munich air disaster in 1958 to the 'Class of 92'. Icons like the late Sir Bobby Charlton, who passed in 2023, Eric Cantona and Wayne Rooney, to name a few, have donned the famous red jersey.

While the club has struggled to hit the heights of the 1990s and 2000s since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, they remain level as the most successful club in England - and with three Champions Leagues to their name, one of the best teams to have ever played in Europe, as well. The question is: how much longer will it be before United are fighting for football's biggest trophies again?

A club that needs no introduction. Liverpool Football Club is a footballing household name around the world. Anfield roars with the Reds' anthem of "You'll Never Walk Alone". Adopted courtesy of Gerry and the Pacemakers back in the 1960s, it's a song that transcends boundaries and unites football lovers across the globe.

With 68 trophies, Liverpool's legacy speaks of European nights, iconic comebacks, and legendary figures like Bill Shankly and Kenny Dalglish. Having won their first league title in 30 years in 2020, they only had to wait another five to get their hands on it again, with Arne Slot's debut campaign sending the Reds back to the top of the Premier League thanks to the heroics of stars like Mohamed Salah and Virgil van Dijk.

In football, trophies come with bragging rights. But which English club has won the most silverware in history?

#1348. Allegri: ‘Napoli needed to smile for a goal, McTominay and De Bruyne switched role’

Max Allegri explains the tactical tweaks he made for Scott McTominay and Kevin De Bruyne during Napoli’s 1-0 win over Torino, not to mention his advice. ‘Try smiling and we might get a goal.’

The Partenopei struggled to get the better of Torino at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, and were rescued by the woodwork when Rolando Mandragora’s screamer surprised Vanja Milinkovic-Savic just before half-time.

However, McTominay got the only goal of the game when Noa Lang turned a defensive run into an attacking one, setting up the Scotland international on the edge of the area.

It was noted on the touchline that after the goal, Allegri turned to his bench and said this was because he had told the players to smile more.

“The mood wasn’t right because we had so many chances, I told them at half-time to try smiling and we might get a goal,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

“They did really well to win this game, while suffering against a strong opponent. Perhaps it is positive that we won under pressure, but we also should’ve done better controlling the tempo, moving the ball from one side to the other.

“The lads did very well in defending on set plays and corner kicks.”

It came at a cost, as Napoli’s injury crisis intensified further with Antonio Vergara limping off just 11 minutes into the game, meaning there was barely any rest for De Bruyne ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League trip to Manchester City.

At first, De Bruyne was in the more advanced role behind Rasmus Hojlund, but after a few minutes Allegri dropped the Belgium international deeper and put McTominay there instead.

“The fun thing about this job is finding solutions. I am starting to get to know these players, I thought De Bruyne could do better as a support for the striker, but in this situation, McTominay was more useful,” explained the coach.

“I just told McTominay not to be already in the position right behind Hojlund, but to run into that space, as it would make him harder to mark. If he is already there and not mobile, then obviously he’s going to be easier to control, but he started to move between the lines and did better.

“I think Hojlund had a good game, he worked for the team. In football, sometimes things go well in one situation, then go badly in another. Today we finally managed to defend with more determination and grit, but then didn’t score as many as before.

“Hojlund scored on international duty last week, he is a very useful player for us.”

Allegri has made history, becoming the first ever coach to amass 1,100 Serie A points, but now he faces a difficult Champions League trip to Manchester City on Tuesday.

“We need to be realistic, because as I said when the fixture list was first drawn up, our Champions League qualification would be decided in the final three matches,” said the coach.

“On Tuesday we need a good performance, try to get a result, but also know that we’ve got to sort our Serie A position first.”

#1347. Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open new opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

#1346. Xabi Alonso Breaks Silence on Cole Palmer’s Angry Actions After Loss vs Leeds

Xabi Alonso has broken his silence after footage emerged online showing Cole Palmer losing his temper with Joao Pedro following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat to Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

The Blues have now slipped to eighth in the Premier League table after failing to hold on to the lead handed to them by summer signing Emmanuel Emegha, who opened the scoring after just 25 minutes.

Chelsea were soon blown out of the water and handed their third defeat in four matches, though, as Noah Okafor struck twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronsen also got in on the act to hand the Lilywhites their first league win at Stamford Bridge since December 1999.

The inquest into what went wrong, and why confidence has seemingly deserted Chelsea in recent weeks, continues. While the defence has borne the brunt of much of the criticism, with only three teams in the league having conceded more goals this season, Palmer has not covered himself in glory either, following up a largely fruitless creative display with his actions at full-time.

At full-time, Chelsea players went to applaud those fans who had stayed until the end, but Palmer could be spotted seething as he made a bee-line to the tunnel.

His decision to avoid clapping the home support prompted coach Willie Isa and injured teammate Joao Pedro to intervene and try to change his mind. Careful to mask his words with his hand, Palmer strutted up to teammate Pedro with a raised eyebrow, continuing to look angry as he refused to reconsider. Watch the incident below:

The Blues continue to struggle for consistency this season and now sit eighth in the Premier League table.

This weekend's result was made even more damaging by the fact Moises Caicedo had to be taken off through injury in the first-half. The Blues may find some solace in the form of back-to-back fixtures against relegation candidates Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace, but they then face the daunting task of turning their form around against Liverpool and Manchester City.

Alonso - who now finds himself under growing pressure in the Stamford Bridge hot seat - was asked about Palmer's full-time actions, to which he responded to the media (watch below):

“We were disappointed, the fans were disappointed. We understand their frustration because expectations are high, and we feel sorry for them. We are in a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together. There is still a long way to go.”

It would seem the Spaniard was eager to stay away from the controversy, having been more concerned about trying to turn his side's form around.

On Chelsea struggling to respond to setbacks, he added: “That's our job, to find solutions and learn from bad experiences like today. We need to improve our ability to overcome difficult moments during games. It's a very important part of our progression.”

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1345. Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this new and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

Ross Barkley heads Aston Villa into the lead against Viking 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/gCFfr2iiVr

Barkley has now been involved in six goals in his last three starts and continues to prove a valuable and unsung member of Emery’s squad.Villa were now dominant, with Viking struggling to repel the constant pressure. Last week Viking marked their home debut in the Champions League by securing a famous 3-3 draw with heavyweights Bayern Munich. They had led 2-0 at half-time before rescuing a point in the last minute.

Hopes of another famous European night here never appeared likely, even though their 2,500 travelling supporters remained noisy all evening.

Villa were awarded a second goal after Alysson was brought down in the penalty area by Zlatko Tripic.

The spot kick was awarded more than a minute after the actual incident following a recommendation from VAR, with Austrian referee Sebastian Gishamer watching it again on the TV monitor. Emiliano Buendía calmly dispatched the penalty to put Villa in total control.

#1344. Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

City were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

There is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ said Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83)

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca said. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of big chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

#1343. Newcastle Wasted a Fortune on Bazoumana Toure, Jaissle Doesn't Rate Him

Newcastle United hosted Arsenal in the Premier League on Saturday evening, and fans were not happy about the state of the team even before a ball was kicked.

The Magpies started with a team that looked very weak on paper, including young midfielders Seun Steur and Lewis Miley playing, with Joe Willock in midfield, and Jacob Murphy in attack alongside William Osula and Harvey Barnes.

The substitutes' bench saw much stronger options available, including the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Anthony Elanga, Nico Gonzalez, Yoanne Wissa, Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey, and Sven Botman.

But perhaps more significantly was the fact that two summer signings in Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure were not included in the matchday squad at all by Matthias Jaissle, despite the club spending £72m on the pair under Eddie Howe.

Neither player was expected to be ready to make an immediate impact on the starting lineup this season considering their age, profile, and experience at the top level. But to not be included in the squad at all, despite the clear issues that the squad is having this season, suggests that the manager has no faith in their qualities.

It's also worth noting that Newcastle were without Joelinton for the game, with the Brazilian injured and unavailable for selection. That would imply that both players are even further down the pecking order than it may seem initially.

Bamba's lack of involvement is potentially not as worrying, because of the options in midfield. Steur has been pushing for an opportunity, and with Nico Gonzalez on the bench, and Jaissle a huge fan of Willock, him being left out on this occasion can be excused.

But for Toure, the situation is hugely different. Newcastle have been struggling for goals all season, managing just 13 goals in their 10 games before the Arsenal fixture, and their top scorers Barnes, Willock, and Elanga all have just two goals each.

Other attacking options in the squad have struggled to make any sort of impact too, while Toure has two goals this season despite having started just one game in all competitions. His incredible pace, dribbling ability, and creativity should mean that he should at least be considered by a manager looking for ways to turn the team's fortunes around.

When Newcastle agreed a £42m deal to sign Toure from Hoffenheim, it was with the idea of him becoming an integral part of the future of the club under Eddie Howe.

But before the season even began Howe had left, and it now looks evident that Toure is not someone that Jaissle wants as part of his squad.

The Ivorian hasn't started a game since August, and despite the team winning just three of their opening ten games in the Premier League, he can't get a look in. Jaissle has no interest in giving Toure an opportunity at this point, and his exclusion from the squad against Arsenal proves it.

If Newcastle had known that Jaissle was going to come in and not be a fan of Toure, then there is no way they would have committed such a large fee to bringing him into the club just to be sidelined. It's a huge oversight on behalf of the board, and it's a massive waste of money too.

Matthias Jaissle is keen to strengthen his squad in the January transfer window

#1341. Nobody is Talking About The Tottenham Star Who Must Be Axed After 2-0 Win vs Ipswich

Tottenham Hotspur returned to winning ways with a dominant 2-0 win over Ipswich in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.

Luca Williams-Barnett took all the headlines as he scored the opening goal and then set up Dominic Solanke for the second, helping the Lilywhites to their fourth win in five games in the top flight.

The youngster was handed his first start for the club, as Roberto De Zerbi admitted that a number of factors had led to the decision, and also contributed to a number of other changes being made to the starting lineup for the clash.

Sandro Tonali missed out due to illness, while Mathys Tel has been ruled out until next month with an ankle injury. Destiny Udogie, Conor Gallagher, James Maddison, and Solanke all also earned starts after missing out last time, with Andy Robertson, Archie Gray, Omar Marmoush, Tel and Tonali all dropping out.

But there was a more unexpected change in the defence for the game too, with Marcos Senesi coming in alongside Jan Paul van Hecke, with Micky Van de Ven dropping to the bench.

Van de Ven played 90 minutes in both of the Netherlands fixtures during the international break, as they claimed a 7-0 win over Greece before being crushed 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp's Germany, but despite being fit and available, he was left out against the Tractor Boys.

Spurs didn't miss him in the slightest, however, as the Argentina international stepped into the side and turned in a brilliant performance to help unlock the low block of Gary O'Neil's side with his excellent passing out from the back and reading of the game.

It was the third time this season that Van Hecke and Senesi have started together, and it was their first win, having previously played in the 3-0 defeat to Brentford on the opening day, and the 1-1 draw against Man Utd at Old Trafford.

But the draw against United should have been a comfortable win but for some poor finishing from the forwards, and this performance against Ipswich was among the best the team have had this season. It's no coincidence that the control of the team was far more stable with Senesi in the side, and it now looks like he should be keeping his place in the team.

With the way that De Zerbi wants to play, control is paramount. Van de Ven is a top defender, and the club clearly rates him highly after handing him a bumper new contract in the summer.

But Senesi has shown, whenever he has played, that he is more of a fit for the manager's plans and style, and that is now leading to an uncomfortable conversation about him being in the team ahead of the captain.

If the manager is serious about creating an environment and atmosphere in the squad that is competitive, then he shouldn't be afraid to drop big names when he has other players who are outperforming them.

If Van de Ven is the leader that the club see him as, then he should react to the decision to leave him out by stepping up in training and being ready to claim his place back. Senesi deserves his spot in the side, and his performance proves it. Now it's on De Zerbi to make the decision to actually pull the trigger.

Tottenham are set to take a close look at Stade de Reims ace Yaya Fofana in action this weekend following a stunning season in front of goal

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. In the end, much to the frustration of Newcastle and Ashley, he said no.”

Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1339. Serie A: Juventus vs. Venezia – probable line-ups, where to watch on TV

Juventus look to Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani in attack as they host struggling Venezia in a must-win game at the Allianz Stadium.

The Bianconeri are still dealing with an injury crisis, but Andrea Cambiaso and Zeki Celik are available, and the Turkishman is competing with Federico Gatti for a starting spot in a back three, as Sky and Gazzetta report.

Francisco Conceiçao is also back from an injury, but not fit to start, so he might be introduced in the second half.

Other key players such as Kenan Yildiz, Nico Gonzalez, Khephren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli remain sidelined with injuries.

Venezia have also travelled to Turin without several players, including ex-Lazio man Toma Basic and Pasquale Mazzocchi. Basic’s absence means USMNT midfielder Gianluca Busio will start in the middle of the park, joining Kike Perez and Simon Sohm.

The match will be broadcast live on TNT Sports 1 in the UK and Ireland, DAZN and HBO Max. Paramount+ will show the game in the USA; Football Italia will provide live updates via a live blog.

Juventus (3-4-2-1): Vicario; Gatti, Bremer, Lucumì; McKennie, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners, Cabal; Kolo Muani, Alajbegovic; Woltemade.

Venezia (3-5-2): F. Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Juan Jesus; Hainaut, Perez, Sohm, Busio, Haps; Adams, Yeboah

#1338. Forget Konsa: Aston Villa's Biggest Mistake Was Selling Donyell Malen

Aston Villa were held to a 0-0 draw against relegation-battling Sunderland on Saturday afternoon, as Unai Emery's side continued their mixed start to the campaign.

The Villans have won just three of their first 11 games in the Premier League this season after the result at Villa Park, leaving them in 11th place in the table, despite having seen the majority of their starting lineup depart during the summer transfer window.

Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea, Youri Tielemans joined Man Utd, Lucas Digne joined Paris Saint-Germain, Ezri Konsa joined Arsenal, Ollie Watkins joined Al-Hilal, and Emi Martinez joined Chelsea, leaving Emery incredibly short of experience and familiarity within his squad.

Emery brought in 10 new players during the summer window to help replace them and strengthen the squad, but the team have struggled to adapt and the results have not been as forthcoming as they would have hoped.

But while Konsa has gone from strength to strength since his move to the Emirates Stadium, establishing himself as one of the best central defenders in the Premier League, the lack of goals in the side has been more of a problem.

Watkins' departure has left a major hole in the side, and while Nicolas Jackson's performances have been largely good, that reliable threat of scoring regularly seems to have gone.

But what is not being spoken about enough is the fact that Aston Villa also allowed Donyell Malen to leave the club permanently in the summer, and he would be the perfect solution to a lot of the issues they are currently having.

The Netherlands international has been in remarkable form since joining AS Roma on an initial loan deal in the January transfer window, scoring 25 goals in Serie A - 12 more than the next-best players in Marcus Thuram and Anastasios Douvikas.

The forward extended his place at the top of that chart with a stunning performance on Saturday night as he scored four goals in their win over Parma, and showed Aston Villa exactly what they are missing in their current side.

“He is strong, inside the area he is devastating.

“He has quickness in his control, in moving the ball, in shooting, and he is composed in front of goal. For us he is an extra weapon. We are keeping him close and we hope he continues like this in these last two matches.”

When Malen signed for Aston Villa, he had a reputation for being a goalscoring winger with great pace, but Emery seemed to never fully trust him, and ultimately his place in the team was never assured.

Now that he has gone over to Italy, he is showing what could have happened if he had been given that trust. He is scoring goals for fun in a league that is best known for its defensive qualities, and is making it look easy.

If Emery had ever given him that opportunity, then it may be that the sale of Watkins wouldn't have been such an issue. They would have already had a reliable source of goals in the squad, and there would be less pressure on Jackson and youngster Brian Madjo to hit the ground running.

The manager allowed several key players to leave in the summer, but it now seems clear that his biggest mistake was letting Malen leave and not replacing him properly.

With key injuries depleting options but no place for Garnacho, Villa contemplate cancelling the loan in January.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Couldn't agree more. I think Emery is a superb coach and am delighted with what he has achieved so far at my beloved club. However, failing to recognise huge potential in some players (Malen is one of several) is seriously affecting Villa's results and subsequent progression.

Yes im inclined to agree emery made massive mistake in letting him go cus look how he's smashing them in at Roma unai should have kept him cus we already had a perfect replacement for wakins in him would have saved the club alot of money cus jackson aint no 20 goals a season forward

#1337. Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

#1336. O'Neill hails recalled midfield duo Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan after both net to help sink St Mirren

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

O’Neill said: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill said: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

‘I thought he did very well,’ said O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ said McLeish.

‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’

#1335. ‘I Played For Both Man Utd and Liverpool - Here’s Which is the Bigger Club’

A former Premier League star who represented both Manchester United and Liverpool has named the club he believes is bigger, offering his verdict on a debate that shows no signs of going away anytime soon.

The Reds, thanks to the hugely successful managerial reigns of Bill Shankly, Bob Paisley and, more recently, Jurgen Klopp, are the most successful club in English football history, having won a joint-record 20 league titles, as well as twice as many Champions League trophies as their fierce rivals 30 miles east.

However, with the Red Devils enjoying the most dominant period of the modern era, winning 11 league titles under Sir Alex Ferguson during a time when football's commercial landscape was rapidly evolving, the argument from their corner is that they boast more social media followers, a larger global fanbase and, consequently, greater financial muscle in the transfer market, alongside a bigger stadium.

Clearly, this is no open-and-shut case. With plenty of grey areas when it comes to measuring the overall size of a football club, one former player who experienced life at both sides of the divide once attempted to settle the score, even bringing Real Madrid into the conversation for good measure.

Paul Ince - one of England's greatest midfielders ever - played 81 times for Liverpool and 281 times for Man United. Revealing his pick for the bigger club out of the two, he said, as per All Football:

"Man United's got to be the biggest club, as much as I love Liverpool. From a historical point of view, Man United with the Busby Babes, all the stuff that's gone on historically.

From winning trophies... Liverpool had their time with European Cups and that, but I think if you looked at the biggest club, even from a financial point of view, you'd say Manchester United is the club that everybody talks about globally. There's Liverpool, Man United and Real Madrid but the biggest club has got to be Man United."

Liverpool and Man United have both won countless trophies over the years.

Ince played for the Red Devils from 1989 to 1995 under manager Sir Alex Ferguson, helping end the club's four-year trophy drought and 22-year top-flight title wait in the 1992/93 season, which also saw him win the club's Player of the Year award.

A year later, he would help United retain that title, adding to a trophy cabinet that also consisted of a League Cup (1992), and the European Cup Winners' Cup (1991).

Michael Owen is the most famous example of players to have represented both sides. The former Liverpool striker became a household name at Anfield, scoring 158 goals in 297 appearances and winning the Ballon d'Or in 2001. After spells at Real Madrid and Newcastle United, he moved to Old Trafford in 2009, where he spent three seasons, winning a Premier League title in 2010/11.

Other notable players include Peter Beardsley, who played for United early in his career before becoming a Liverpool star in the late 1980s, and Phil Chisnall, who made the controversial move directly from United to Liverpool in 1964.

Who does AI rank as the 20 biggest clubs in British football history?

More recently, Gabriel Heinze was set to play for both clubs, although his proposed move from United to Liverpool in 2007 was famously blocked by Sir Alex Ferguson, with the Argentine instead joining Real Madrid.

There have also been players such as Tom Chorlton, Arthur Riley and Fred Hopkin who crossed between the clubs during earlier periods of their histories.

#1333. Rio Ferdinand Named 3 Liverpool Players he 'Hated' on the Pitch

By virtue of Manchester United’s size and stature, they have many rivals. From the likes of Leeds United – now back in England’s top tier – to their clashes with Barcelona, which will never lose its significance, there is no shortage of teams who relish the competition.

None compare to their undying, hatred-filled meetings with Liverpool, however, who – alongside the Red Devils – are considered to be one of the greatest footballing institutions in the country and the world.

At the epicentre of the rivalry is the likes of Rio Ferdinand who, expectedly, picked out three former players of the Merseyside-based outfit when naming the five players who he hated the most during his illustrious playing days on his YouTube channel.

Mario Balotelli is a figure in football who is never too far away from controversy. The Premier League got their first taste of the maverick when he joined Manchester City in 2010 – and well, he made himself known, according to Ferdinand.

“I hated Balotelli, hated him,” Ferdinand said. “He did a couple of things I didn’t like with the fans, and I thought he was rude.

“But I chat with him now, lovely geezer. It’s mad because I’d see him after, and it would only be respectful. In the games, he was a different animal on the pitch. In the end, I respected it.”

A 36-cap, 14-goal Italy international also turned out for Liverpool between 2014 and 2016. Balotelli's most memorable match against the Old Trafford-based outfit was, in fact, Manchester City's 6-1 victory in the 2011/12 campaign. The striker scored two that day.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Balotelli has just one Premier League assist to his name - that was the winning pass for Sergio Aguero to win the title against QPR.

Mario Balotelli - Record against Ferdinand

Ferdinand had the displeasure of keeping tabs on former Barcelona and Liverpool talisman Luis Suarez on just five occasions, reigning victorious in three of those but fans cannot doubt that the Uruguayan centre forward was a sensational marksman during his 133-game stint on Merseyside.

From Luis Suarez to the incredible Pele, here are the most intelligent strikers of all-time.

He was, however, no stranger to rubbing up opponents the wrong way. The defender’s teammate Patrice Evra, a Frenchman of African descent, accused the striker of being racist during the 2011/12 campaign, which led to the Englishman refusing to shake his hands when they next locked horns.

Now-pundit Ferdinand also 'hated' the long-haired Fernando Torres and opened up about a moment when the Spaniard stamped on him off the ball, which left him with stitches in his foot. The ex-central defender said:

"Didn’t like Torres. He stamped on my foot one time when the ball was up the other end, stitches in my foot. I was playing, the ball was in the other end, we had some tussles - he was game - he just stamped on my foot, no ball about anywhere.

“Went in at half-time, took off my boot and it was the worst thing I could’ve done," he continued. "My foot went, ‘Woof’, I need stitches. I had an injection. For ages it was killing me, got a scar on my foot.”

Torres – regarded as one of the best players not to win the English top flight – was a serious threat during his days at Anfield, notching 81 strikes across 142 outings, but struggled to emulate the same goalscoring ability for Chelsea.

Fernando Torres - Record against Ferdinand

Midfielder-turned-pundit Robbie Savage is considered to be one of the biggest wind-up merchants in Premier League history. Wrexham-born, he did absolutely everything in his power to try and end up on the winning side during a match. Ferdinand said:

"I hated Robbie Savage. I'm mates with him now, I love him. He's a lovely guy!"

Since their respective retirements, Savage and Ferdinand have become friends, having crossed paths in the punditry world. Their rivalry may be over, but Premier League aficionados will always fondly remember the pair of Brits locking horns during the peak top flight years.

Kevin Davies, formerly of Bolton Wanderers and Southampton, was an extremely physical presence on the turf and somewhat relished the non-football side of the game – as Ferdinand found out on 19 different occasions.

He played a total of 15 years in the Premier League, turning out for an array of clubs, but his record against the Manchester United stalwart makes for grim reading. In 19 outings, equating to 1,471 minutes of action, the once-capped England international won just four times.

#1332. Watford Sack Manager Alessio Dionisi After Sheffield United Defeat

Watford have sacked manager Alessio Dionisi following their heavy defeat away to Sheffield United at the weekend.

The Hornets have won just three times in their last 13 games, and despite two strong results ahead of their game against the Blades, time is expected to be up for Dionisi.

Watford currently sit just outside the relegation zone on 15 points, having won just four times in the Championship all season.

Their away form has been particularly concerning so far this campaign, picking up just one point from their eight games on the road.

Watford were 2-0 down after just eight minutes against Sheffield United, but they barely laid a glove on their opponents despite chasing the game for almost 90 minutes.

They produced just seven shots with a total of 0.32 xG, having just nine touches inside the opposition box.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Watford have sacked manager Dionisi following their 4-0 defeat away to Sheffield United.

The Hornets have won just three times in their last 13 games, and although Watford tried to give him the benefit of the doubt and support after losing 4-0 against Burnley and 5-1 against Cardiff City, his position has now become untenable.

Sources say that Dionisi was liked as a person internally at the club, but a lack of identity in their style of play, poor in-game management, and failing to know his best starting XI are all factors as to why he's been relieved of his duties.

GIVEMESPORT reported back in October that Watford are aware that they've been too hasty in the past when it comes to sacking managers, and were looking to give Dionisi a little more time.

Unfortunately, the defeat against Sheffield United was the final straw for Dionisi, with Watford still searching for their first win of the season away from home.

The Championship is home to some massive football clubs in England, but which stadiums in the division have the highest attendance based on capacity?

Speaking after the heavy defeat against Sheffield United, Dionisi apologised to the supporters.

"I'm sorry for our supporters. Because when we play away, we play without courage and we weren't aggressive; it's impossible. When you play away against Sheffield United or any club, it's impossible when you play without courage and without personality."

Dionisi must have known the writing was on the wall for him following the heavy defeat.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Dionisi has been hanging on to his job by a thread for several weeks now, and the result against Sheffield United was clearly the final straw.

It's unclear what direction Watford are going to turn in now, but with a five-point cushion above the drop zone, their season is far from over.

#1330. The right to do wrong
